verdictSummary: One required finding, RF1: the parent renders the step-4 write/read grant from the step-3 child's mutable output root. With RF1 corrected and a real-sandbox regression test added, the reviewed evidence supports ACCEPT-UNIT for the concrete adapter and fixed macOS development host profile. A narrow delta review is needed. Not hermetic, not product integration, not release/runtime qualification.

scope.trustModel: Parent/admission Python, the host kernel, sandbox-exec/system.sb, dyld and system libraries are the explicit reviewed TCB. Child steps (Python preparation code/modules, Node scripts and TypeScript package, Rust generator binary) are treated as untrusted for confinement.
scope.notReaudited: General architecture; the original Typify/pure-dependency algorithms accepted earlier.

NR1.evidence: validate_options and flatten refuse denied refs and any denied+'/' prefix. The real CLI with --write refuses P5 (options-level HelloV3/properties/protocolMajor). A nested $ref into HelloV3/properties/protocolMajor added to a selected native definition (sources/source-map/closure rebound) is refused inside the confined Python child. Outputs unchanged in both cases. The TS facade refuses direct, nested and trailing-slash superseded refs.

NR2.evidence: The policy row subjectDeclaredFeatures={} is enforced. Real cargo metadata refuses both an inactive serde/rc forwarding feature and an empty local feature; the unmodified workspace passes with 11 dependencies. The fixture tests pass.

A1.evidence: prettyplease replaces rustfmt, nativeLibraries=[], and the generator links only libSystem. The Python child is confined with exact interpreter/library/25 .py + 3 .so grants. The parent interpreter and entrypoint are declared TCB, not self-verified trust.

A2.evidence: The receipt join checks sources, builder, dependencies, profile flags and executable. An independent clean vendor build (network denied) produced a different hash (6b35cbaf…) whose 8 output bodies are byte-identical to the frozen outputs.

A7.evidence: Child stdout/stderr are captured; success prints exactly one JSON line (real runs and --write).

A8.evidence: Nine stub execution tests exist; stubs bypass sandbox-exec by design. The real-sandbox behaviour was independently exercised (probes A-G).

NA1.evidence: convert() compares nested $id/$schema; test and code confirmed.

NA2.evidence: createReportShapeRegistry exposes a frozen {checkEntryPoints, matches} limited to the 586 selected refs.

NA3.evidence: All 28 pins match the architecture checkout, but they bind worktree bytes (see ADV2).

NA5.evidence: validate-schemas writes schema-runtime.cjs into runtime-scratch, not inputs.

requiredFindings.title: Step-4 confinement grant is derived from the step-3 child's mutable output root
requiredFindings.location: tools/generate_contracts.py:72-81 (child_profile) and :394-405 (run: shared output, quote()=Path.resolve(strict=True) at render time)
requiredFindings.detail: The Node/Rust child_profile grants file-write* and file-read* on (subpath output), which includes the root literal. The generator child (step 3) can rmdir the root and create a symlink at work/output pointing to any existing directory. The parent then renders the TypeScript child's (step 4) profile with Path(output).resolve(strict=True), so step 4 is granted read and write on the symlink target. The Python child's profile already excludes its root literal; the Node/Rust profile does not. The parent's O_NOFOLLOW collection then refuses publication, but the outside effect has already happened. The step-2 child can likewise replace runtime-scratch (demonstrated), which is currently harmless because scratch is only used as cwd.

evidence.control: Real generator plus a probe TS child: read, create and overwrite of the victim are all EPERM.
evidence.escape: Symlinking generator stub plus the same probe TS child: victim canary read ALLOWED, new file written ALLOWED, canary overwritten ('victim canary\ntampered\n'). The parent exits 1; checked-in outputs are unchanged.
evidence.honestStep4: An honest generate-ts.cjs got EPERM traversing the symlink path, so a single malicious step-3 child alone did not produce outside writes. The escape needs a step-4 child that targets the resolved path.
evidence.fixValidated: In a rebound copy, a write grant of (require-all (subpath p) (require-not (literal p))) blocks the escape (all victim operations EPERM). Real four-step generation with the same change still publishes bodies identical to the frozen outputs.

requiredFindings.correction: Make every child write root parent-owned and non-replaceable, and never derive a later grant from child-mutable state. Minimum: exclude the root literal from Node/Rust write grants (as the Python profile does). Before rendering each subsequent profile, lstat-check that output/scratch are still the parent-created directories (same st_dev/st_ino, not symlinks). Preferably give steps 3 and 4 distinct fresh output roots and render all profiles from paths resolved once before any child runs. Add a real sandbox-exec regression test (not the stub runner) where step 3 replaces its root and step 4 attempts an outside read/write.

advisories.title: report.ts still exports generic SchemaRegistry/parseExact/canonical
advisories.detail: The embedded selected bytes are reachable only through the frozen facade (all 9 probe refs and all 4 unselected definitions refused; facade mutation ineffective). Consumers can still construct their own SchemaRegistry. Either document it as a generic inert API or stop exporting it from the report output.

advisories.title: Architecture pins bind worktree bytes, not a commit
advisories.detail: All 28 source-map pins match /Users/sb/code/opensip-ai/opensip_arch bytes. At HEAD c3856824…, 22 of the paths are untracked and 3 are modified. Integration binding should name a committed/reviewed architecture revision or an equivalent frozen manifest.

advisories.title: Parent could re-derive owners.json
advisories.detail: owners.json from the confined Python child flows into the generator without comparison. The parent can cheaply require exactly json.dumps(options['owners'], indent=2)+'\n'. Integrity currently rests on pinned prepare code.

advisories.title: Receipt join is narrow and non-reproducible
advisories.detail: validate_build_receipt does not check tools/versions/target/python/environment/command fields against anything. It records an observed trusted-host build, not an attestation. Nine dependency build scripts and three proc-macros run unconfined on the trusted host at build time (prettyplease build.rs reviewed: benign).

advisories.title: Resource limits
advisories.detail: Fork and exec are denied in all child profiles (probes A, C, D), so the 300 s timeout kill covers the whole child. CPU/memory/disk use inside granted roots is unbounded until the 128 MiB collection check. The timeout path was reviewed in code, not triggered.

advisories.title: Witness provenance record
advisories.detail: validation-03 witness-source.json names the trial-02 corpus (533f82b7…). The file actually used (d79f78e0…) is that corpus minus the 5 superseded rows with identical values. Record the derived file digest.

selectedInputGenerationObligations.metWithinExplicitTCB: Yes for the exact selected inputs, except the RF1 cross-step confinement defect.
details: Source/options/output-role/vocabulary guards refuse all exercised mutations (22 generation tests plus independent CLI probes).

Four real child steps run under sandbox-exec. Outside reads/writes, input/code writes, hardlinks, network (TCP, UDP, DNS, mDNSResponder, syslog), fork and exec are denied. Symlink/fifo/extra outputs are refused by the collector without reading outside bytes.
The Python child is strict: unpinned stdlib (csv, socket) cannot import, fork/exec are EPERM, and its root cannot be removed.
Malformed Python-profile, confinement, hostProfile and nativeLibraries mutations are refused with controlled GenerationError before any child runs.
Publishing preflight: a hard-linked destination is replaced without touching outside bytes, a symlinked generated directory refuses before any write, and stdout is one JSON line.
A fresh 8-output drift check on the frozen copy with the real binaries is clean.
The TS outputs pass a strict tsc compile, and all 1338 selected witnesses pass Rust roundtrip and TS original-schema matching.

remainingBootstrapCheckBeforeIntegration: An external reviewed anchor (the inventory/design-lock successor, not these self hashes) must select registry 4cf6dbd5… plus recipe contracts-v1, whose generatorClosureSha256 3473abef… covers options 1719ef18…, source-map 561cf9ef…, build receipt and generator executable 0a49cfc4…, node 1ee75375… and python b502cb4c…. Its 28 architecture sources must be pinned at a committed architecture revision. verify_design currently carries the accepted predecessor lock and does not select these rows. Then the protocol/report source-closure owners, and other platform/release qualification, remain integration obligations.
limits: macOS 26.6.2 aarch64 development host only. sandbox-exec/system.sb, kernel, dyld, CoreFoundation/Security, Homebrew Python and nvm Node are trusted, and the files are only integrity-checked before and after.
No hermeticity, reproducible-build or release/runtime claim. A malicious host user racing native files is out of scope.
Seatbelt behaviour was observed empirically on this OS build; SBPL semantics are undocumented.
Timeout expiry and memory/disk exhaustion were not triggered.
Linux and other targets were not examined.
Witness results are finite observations, not semantic admission.
